title: SDK transport: request-slicing, idle socket lifecycle, and per-route pooling examples
creator: Ava Chen
description: Problem: Customer apps with mixed short-polling and long-streaming workloads see high socket churn and uneven tail latencies. Current SDK defaults open large per-route connection pools and long keepalive windows which increase ephemeral connection counts and cost on small app instances. Goal: Provide concrete cross-SDK guidance and code examples (Python, TypeScript, Go) for request slicing, per-route pooling, idle socket lifecycle (TCP LINGER/keepalive), and safe defaults for streaming + retries so teams can reduce connection churn, improve P95/P99 latency, and maintain streaming ergonomics.
acceptance_criteria: Publish a short SDK guide page with language-specific examples integrated into SDK docs
Default transport presets added to Python/TS/Go SDKs behind opt-in feature flag
Automated tests demonstrating stable streaming reconnects with <=1% error amplification under simulated transient network failures
Bench results: reduce average ephemeral connection churn by >=30% on mixed workload benchmark, holding median latency +/-5%
Telemetry: new metrics emitted for per-route active_sockets and idle_cycle_count
design_notes: Principles: (1) favor fewer long-lived connections over many short ones for same host; (2) separate pools by workload shape (short requests vs streaming); (3) conservative timeouts to avoid early request cancellation but fail fast for retryable client errors; (4) preserve streaming semantics: immediate backpressure and deterministic reconnect behavior.
Request slicing: for large user payload uploads or long prompt preprocessing, surface a 'slice' API pattern in SDKs that uses a single connection and windowed writes to avoid spiky socket bursts.
Per-route pools: add per-route pool-sizing that defaults to min(4, cpu_count) for short RPCs and dedicated streaming pool size 2. Allow explicit override via TransportOptions.pool_config.

Idle lifecycle: reduce OS-level TIME_WAIT and ephemeral port exhaustion by using keepalive probes (interval 60s, probes 3) and an SDK-level idle_reap window of 120s for short-pool sockets; streaming pool keeps sockets 15m by default.

Retries & streaming: implement idempotent-aware retries and a streaming reconnect handshake that resumes from last acknowledged token id. Non-idempotent calls use client-side deduplication tokens when safe.
per_language_examples:
Python: TransportOptions(pool_config={"short":4,"stream":2}, keepalive=(60,3), idle_reap_s=120)
Example: client = RedwoodClient(transport=HttpTransport(TransportOptions(...)))
Streaming: client.stream(..., reconnect_policy=ResumeTokenPolicy())

TypeScript: const transport = new Transport({ pools: { short: 4, stream: 2 }, keepalive: { intervalMs: 60000, probes: 3 }, idleReapMs: 120000 })
client = new RedwoodClient({ transport })
Streaming: client.stream({ onResumeToken: (t) => { /* store token */ } })

Go: opts := transport.DefaultOptions()
opts.Pools.Short = 4
opts.Pools.Stream = 2
opts.Keepalive.Interval = 60*time.Second
opts.Keepalive.Probes = 3
opts.IdleReap = 120*time.Second
client := redwood.NewClient(redwood.WithTransport(opts))
Streaming: stream, err := client.Stream(ctx, req); stream.SetResumeHandler(resumeHandler)
telemetry_and_metrics: New metrics emitted by SDKs (names tentative): sdk.transport.active_sockets{pool=short|stream,lang=python|ts|go}
sdk.transport.idle_reap_count - counts sockets closed by idle reaper
sdk.transport.reconnect_attempts - streaming reconnect attempts per session
key dashboards: per-route socket count (host+route), ephemeral_port_pressure gauge, request_latency_p99_by_route
Prototype numbers (local perf lab): mixed benchmark (50% short requests 150ms, 50% streams) -> ephemeral connection churn down 38%, p99 tail latency improved 12% under network jitter scenario
test_plan: Unit: options parsing and validation across three SDKs
Integration: end-to-end tests against transport simulator that injects 50-200ms packet loss and randomized 1-3s dropouts; assert streaming reconnect < 1s and <1% duplicate messages
Load: run mixed workload benchmark with small app instance (2 vCPU) comparing baseline vs new presets; collect socket churn and latency distribution
E2E: validate resume tokens across client restarts and server-side KV cache correlation
Canary: behind feature flag rollout to 5% of Hosted API traffic, monitor active_sockets and error budget metrics
